name: NuSTAR
summary: Focusing hard-X-ray observatory whose Galactic-center and M31 observations test radiatively decaying sterile-neutrino dark matter.
detection_principle: Hard-X-ray focusing optics and energy-resolving detectors measure narrow spectral lines. Unfocused photons and instrumental backgrounds must also be modeled.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: NASA's current mission page labels the observatory an “Active Mission.”

collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

key_parameters.name: Exposure in the representative M31 analysis

results.summary: Galactic-center X-ray searches constrain radiative sterile-neutrino decay.
Deep M31 exposures provide independent constraints.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
